title: Population
description: Reference schema for docs/timeline/SPEC.md §7.1's Population node type — biological/demographic units (hominin lineages, ancient-DNA clusters). Entities aggregate claims; they assert nothing on their own — every substantive statement about a Population lives in a linked Claim (subject_type: Population, subject_id: this entity's id), not inline here. The hand-rolled validator (docs/timeline/scripts/validate-timeline.mjs) is authoritative if this file and the validator diverge.

name.description: Common name used across the app, e.g. 'Homo erectus'. Taxonomic disputes go in taxonomic_status, not in alternate id fields.

date_range.description: The population's attested existence window. This is itself claim-shaped data (has its own date_semantics) because the boundary dates are exactly the kind of thing that gets revised by new finds (e.g., Jebel Irhoud 2017 pushing Homo sapiens' earliest attestation back by ~100,000 years) — never presented as a fixed fact independent of the evidence that established it.

latest.description: null for populations understood to persist to the present (e.g. Homo sapiens).

gene_flow_edges.description: SPEC.md §7.1: implements reconnecting branches so interbreeding renders as gene flow, never as tree-violating magic. Each edge additionally requires a backing Claim (subject_type: Population) carrying the sourced percentage/method.

applies_to.description: Which descendant population(s) the percentage is measured in — gene flow percentages vary by population and must not be reported as one global number.

claim_id.description: The Claim that sources this edge.
